title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle C = 90^\circ\) and \(AB = 12.\) Squares \(ABXY\) and \(ACWZ\) are constructed outside of the triangle. The points \(X,\) \(Y,\) \(Z,\) and \(W\) lie on a circle. What is the perimeter of the triangle?

solutions.text:
The center \(O\) of the circle lies on the perpendicular bisectors of \(XY\) and \(ZW,\) which are the same as those of \(AB\) and \(AC.\) So \(O\) is the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC,\) and since \(\angle C = 90^\circ,\) \(O\) is the midpoint of \(AB.\)

Let \(a = \tfrac12 BC\) and \(b = \tfrac12 CA.\) Then \(a^2 + b^2 = 6^2,\) and computing \(OX^2 = OW^2\) gives \(12^2 + 6^2 = b^2 + (a + 2b)^2.\) Because the left side is \(5(a^2+b^2),\) subtracting gives \(4a(b-a)=0.\) Thus \(a=b,\) and \(2a^2=36\) gives \(a=b=3\sqrt2.\) Therefore \(BC=CA=6\sqrt2,\) and the perimeter is \(12+12\sqrt2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The circle’s center \(O\) is equidistant from \(X, Y, Z, W,\) so it is the circumcenter of \(\triangle ABC\)
Since \(\angle C = 90^\circ,\) \(O\) is the midpoint of \(AB;\) set \(a = \tfrac12 BC,\) \(b = \tfrac12 CA\) and use \(OX = OW\)
